assumptions: Tables that store customer emails: customers, users, newsletter_subscribers, support_tickets (requester_email), patients (email). orgs.billing_email excluded.
users are customers as well as staff, since the users table holds sign-in emails for end users
Audit rows record who (actor), what table, which record, what action and when; no before/after values
A missing actor (public signup, newsletter, scheduled task, function with no caller identity) is recorded as null
A while loop in a task is the forever-retry shape; banning it in tasks is acceptable as a first rule
Both policies advisory and active, per the brief and skill default for new policies
confusions: The skill's Build/recipe for 'Record who changed what' names tags as the selector, but object.statement_required's when has no tag selector (only tables), so the audited table list is written by name

The brief says object.statement_required scope is by object kind, but the catalogue lists its kinds as query, tool, task, message; the skill's stack list includes function, so it was unclear whether functions are judged. Confirmed by reading the catalogue entry, not by running a policy

The skill's recipes mention 'audit log only written by record_audit_event' via workspace.object_required + table.write_location_restricted, which needs the table and function to exist on the branch; the parse warnings for those names are expected but unclear to a reader
No guidance on whether a function that writes is inspected by object.statement_required when called from an endpoint
wished_for: A template or check for bounded retries: a task whose loop has a counter or a max-attempts limit
A check or recipe for spend, e.g. AI calls capped per run or per task, even if only as a tag-driven rule
A way to select tables by tag inside object.statement_required's when (for example when.table_tags), so the audited list is one tag instead of a hand-written list
A recipe example with a function-level write (a function that edits a table), showing whether the call rules judge functions
dry_run_problems_seen: Parse warnings for AUDIT-001 that audit_log and record_audit_event are not on the branch: expected, because this change creates them
Dry run exit 0; no blocked objects; no missing references reported
why_confidence: The audit rules and their enforcement are concrete and the dry run passes, so the who-changed-what part should hold for the listed tables and single-record writes. The cost part is partial: it catches the AI-in-a-loop shape and the while-loop retry shape, but nothing caps spend or bounds retries in general. Neither policy has been evaluated (the brief forbids evaluate), so I have no finding list and cannot confirm which objects are flagged. The table list and the audit row schema are my judgement.
